sections.text:
Shuaib, peace be upon him, who is called the “Preacher of the Prophets” due to his extreme eloquence and eloquence, was sent by God to a people who live in the city of “Midian”, an area close to the Levant.

The people of Midian lived in prosperity and bliss thanks to their strategic commercial location through which caravans passed between the Levant, Yemen, and Egypt.

But they took the worst advantage of this blessing, so they disbelieved in God and worshiped a huge tree called “the grove.”

Their corruption was not limited to polytheism, but rather they invented a new type of economic and social corruption. They were turning away the measure and the balance!
If they bought goods from people, they would demand that they be weighed fully and adequately for them, and if they sold goods to people, they would reduce the weight and measure and steal their money falsely.

They also blocked trade caravans, imposed unjust taxes on them, and struck terror in the hearts of travelers.

Prophet Shuaib stood among them like a fruitful tree in the middle of a barren desert, calling them to reform and to unite God in a manner full of compassion and wisdom.

He called them, saying: “O my people, worship God. You have no god but Him, and do not diminish the measure and the balance. I see you are fine, but I fear Upon you is the torment of a terrible day.”

Shuaib warned them that commercial fraud and robbing people would destroy their economy and bring God's wrath and punishment upon them.

He advised them that a small amount of lawful earnings (the rest of God) is better for them than a large amount of unlawful earnings that they accumulate through theft and fraud.

But people who were arrogant about their wealth ridiculed his words and were surprised at how he linked religion to daily commercial transactions.

They said to him sarcastically: “O Shuaib, your origins command us to abandon what our fathers worshiped or to do with our wealth whatever we wish. Indeed, you are the forbearing and the wise.”

Shuaib responded calmly to them that he did not want to disagree with them just because of stubbornness, but rather he wanted to reform their society as much as possible, and that he only trusted in God.

When he convinced them with his argument, they resorted to threats, and said: “If it had not been for your family (your clan), we would have stoned you, and you are not dear to us.”

Shuaib answered them in astonishment: How can they be afraid of his weak human clan, and not fear the powerful, mighty God who disposes of the universe?
Shuaib continued to advise them for a long time, but they persisted in corruption, deception, and disbelief, and they challenged him, saying: “Then drop on us a cloud from the sky if you are of the truthful ones.”

Here came the inevitable end for every unjust people who rejected the advice of their prophets.

God sent upon them an intense heat, with neither water nor shade helpful. The ground was boiling under their feet and the houses were scorching and unbearable.

This stifling heat continued for seven full days, until they saw a huge cloud shadowing an area outside the city.

They were happy and thought that there would be rain and shade that would save them from this hell, so they all went out running and standing under this cloud in search of shade (the torment of the Day of Canopy).

When they all gathered under it, the cloud rained down sparks and blazing fire on them, burning their bodies.

Then followed a loud cry from the sky, and a strong trembling from the earth, and they all perished and became crouched in their homes, as if they had not sung there nor built their trade and civilization.

God saved Shuaib and those who believed with him by His mercy, and they left those lands after God purified them of economic and moral corruption.

The lesson of Shuaib’s story is that commercial fraud and unlawfully consuming people’s money are major sins that destroy societies and destroy nations, and that honesty in transactions is the basis of the blessing of livelihood.
